title: Does the count care how fast you pour? The test as designed

data.source: No data on the question. The only numbers are the test's own pass rates in made-up worlds (2000 repeats each, seed 20261118), adapted from part C of colloquy/lab/epistemic/03_severity.py. Search for real metered data on 2026-11-18: the library's data folders and four Zenodo keyword searches; none found.

prediction: Claim: slope zero. Pass: the 95 per cent interval lies inside plus or minus 0.05. Falsifier: any slope outside. (Regression of log input per cut on log speed, four speeds across a factor of eight.)
baseline: To be used on real data: the leaky integrator (the field's standard model) and the decoy rule "the same time between events at every speed". Not run.
why: Not run. The test needs one real system whose input is metered independently of its events at several steady speeds, and no open data set of that kind was found tonight. A simulated version would only hand back the counting rule typed into it. The design is frozen here with its pass rates. Later the same night another worker found real metered data and ran it: see the books whose slugs begin rt-.
